description:
"Timeless technology, unforgettable stories." We are EV-TRON, a multidisciplinary engineering team from the FP-UNA, focused on winning the Best Storytelling award at NASA Space Apps Asunción 2026.

We tackle the "Abandoned but not Forgotten" challenge by transforming telemetry and technical data from inactive rovers and landers on the Moon and Mars into an immersive digital archaeology platform featuring bilingual poetic narratives, giving a voice back to space exploration's mechanical pioneers.
summary:
EV-TRON is an interactive, bilingual digital archaeology platform designed for K-12 students and educators. Addressing the NASA Space Apps Challenge "Abandoned, but not Forgotten," EV-TRON rescues retired spacecraft, rovers, and deep-space probes from dense technical archives, transforming their legacy into living educational experiences. It was developed by a multidisciplinary team comprising Valeria García, Marketing Engineer from FP-UNA, and Elías Chávez, Electronics Engineer from FP-UNA.

Guided by our friendly robotic archaeologist, EVI-E, users explore an interactive cosmic map that turns cold telemetry and verified NASA NSSDCA open data into engaging, human-centered narratives. EV-TRON is built upon a lightweight, decoupled three-layer architecture: official mission records, accessible scientific breakthroughs, and poetic first-person "last transmissions" available in both English and Spanish, with future localization planned for Guaraní.

Engineered for universal classroom accessibility, our responsive web platform requires zero logins or installations, running seamlessly on both desktop and mobile devices. From Asunción, Paraguay, to schools across the globe, EV-TRON bridges rigorous aerospace engineering with emotional storytelling, inspiring the next generation of explorers to honor the silent pioneers of the cosmos. Because machines built to explore the stars deserve to be remembered.
details:
Storytelling, Art, and Engineering: Why We Built EV-TRON

Science becomes unforgettable when it speaks to the human heart. When children learn about space exploration today, they mostly hear about active missions. Meanwhile, the machines that paved the way—like rovers, landers, descent stages, and deep-space probes—sit inside dense technical databases and textbooks that rarely spark a child's imagination. Those machines taught us how to land, drive, fly, and search for water on other worlds, yet most students have never heard their voices.

To answer NASA's "Abandoned, but not Forgotten" challenge, we created EV-TRON (Echoes of Voyagers, blended with Tron for the digital realm where their signals live on). Our core belief is simple: Timeless technology deserves unforgettable stories.

How It Works: Three Layers of Digital Archaeology

EV-TRON is a lightweight, responsive web platform where EVI-E (Explorer Voice Interface – Educator), our robotic archaeologist, guides students across an interactive map of the Moon, Mars, and deep space. Every retired spacecraft is treated as an archaeological site to excavate, structured into three distinct layers:

  1. Layer 1 — Mission Record: Hard, verifiable engineering parameters (launch dates, planned vs. actual operational lifelines, distances traveled, and current status) linked directly to NASA's official NSSDCA archive.
  2. Layer 2 — The Science: A clear, K-12-friendly explanation translating complex instrumentation into what the spacecraft actually discovered and why it changed space exploration.
  3. Layer 3 — Legacy & Last Transmission: Connects the machine's historical milestone with an evocative, first-person poetic reading narrated by EVI-E in English and Spanish (complete with accessible text transcripts). To uphold strict scientific integrity, EV-TRON clearly separates factual telemetry from poetic interpretation.

Narrative & Bilingual Craft (English & Spanish)

Writing EV-TRON's stories was an exercise in empathy and precision. Rather than relying on literal machine translations, we crafted the English and Spanish narratives independently so each version carries its own natural rhythm, emotional resonance, and clarity for young readers across the Americas and the globe.

Visual Identity & Soundscape

Our visual identity revolves around the concept of "light that endures in the dark." We blend the cold, silent vastness of deep space with the warmth of human storytelling, creating a museum-grade experience that feels both futuristic and deeply emotional.

Typography Strategy

To maintain absolute visual consistency, clean minimalism, and a cutting-edge technological edge, EV-TRON exclusively utilizes the Space Grotesk font family across all design assets. By leveraging different font weights (Bold for high-impact headings, Medium for subtitles, and Normal for body text and telemetry interfaces), we establish a clear, sophisticated hierarchy inspired by modern aerospace telemetry terminals.

Official 6-Color Palette

Our color system is divided into primary structural foundations and secondary narrative accents, incorporating deep cosmic tones and warm Martian red hues drawn directly from our mission environments:

Primary Colors (The Cosmic Foundation & Interface):

  • Deep-Space Canvas (#0B0F1A): The primary background tone representing the boundless void of space and the darkness that makes data shine.
  • Telemetry Cyan (#35E0F2): The core technical accent used for official telemetry, Layer 1 data, and active interactive links.
  • Stellar White (#FFFFFF): Used for primary titles and high-impact headers, bringing the crisp clarity of distant stars.

Secondary Colors (The Narrative & Planetary Accents):

  • Warm Amber (#FF9A3C): The signature tone for EVI-E’s voice, poetic narratives, and key human-centric calls to action.
  • Cosmic Crimson (#C73855): A deep reddish tone extracted from deep-space nebulae and Martian horizons, used for secondary cards and dramatic narrative contrast.
  • Martian Dust (#E07A5F): A warm, grounding terracotta hue inspired by planetary exploration, ideal for subtle background tags and thematic accents.

Technology & Scalability

Built with clean, accessible web standards (HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript) and hosted publicly for instant access on any mobile phone or classroom computer without logins. All mission records and bilingual stories live in an external, structured JSON architecture (stories.json), allowing educators and contributors to add new retired missions—or new languages like Guaraní—in minutes without modifying core application code.

The Team Behind EV-TRON (Asunción, Paraguay)

EV-TRON is the union of two complementary technical and creative worlds from the Facultad Politécnica de la Universidad Nacional de Asunción (FP-UNA):

  • Valeria García (Marketing Engineer, FP-UNA): Led the product strategy, creative direction, visual identity, educational storytelling, bilingual scriptwriting, and user experience (UX/UI), ensuring rigorous science feels warm, human, and globally engaging.
  • Elías Chávez (Electronics Engineer, FP-UNA): Engineered the interactive frontend, decoupled JSON data architecture, responsive layout, and public deployment, transforming raw NASA archival data into a fast, scalable, and robust digital platform.

Our Vision & Future Impact

Beyond the hackathon, we are expanding EV-TRON's archaeological map to include missions like Spirit, Pioneer 10, Kepler, and Dawn, integrating Paraguay's native Guaraní language to honor our roots, and partnering with local schools and science clubs to bring space history into every classroom. Because machines built to explore the stars deserve to be remembered.
